title: Geometric regularity of one fibre descends from maximal target localizations
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, with S an R-algebra and Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Fix a prime ideal p of R and its residue field kappa(p) [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If for every maximal ideal m of S the fibre kappa(p) tensor_R S_m is geometrically regular over kappa(p) [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then kappa(p) tensor_R S is geometrically regular over kappa(p). No flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local), fibre argument in (3) implies (1); checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07C0 on 2026-10-12

proof.text: The fibre F = kappa(p) tensor_R S is Noetherian by Ideal.isNoetherianRing_fiber. For each finite purely inseparable K/kappa(p), K tensor_kappa(p) F is finite over F by Module.Finite.base_change and the tensor commRight equivalence, hence Noetherian by IsNoetherianRing.of_finite. Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange identifies it with K tensor_R S.

For a prime n of K tensor_R S, contract it along includeRight to a prime q of S and choose a maximal m containing q by Ideal.exists_le_maximal. The image M of m.primeCompl under includeRight is disjoint from n, since membership in n contracts to membership in q and then m. IsLocalization.tensorProductEquivOfMapIncludeRight identifies K tensor_R S_m with Localization M. Geometric regularity of the localized fibre, followed by cancelBaseChange, makes this localization regular.

Extend n to Localization M. By the disjointness from M its extension is prime and its contraction is n, using IsLocalization.isPrime_of_isPrime_disjoint and under_map_of_isPrime_disjoint. Mathlib localizationLocalizationAtPrimeIsoLocalization identifies the localization at this extended prime with the localization at n. Transport regular localness through this equivalence and Localization.localRingEquiv for the equality of contracted primes. The regular-ring local criterion proves K tensor_R S regular. Transport back through cancelBaseChange. Together with Noetherianity of F this is geometric regularity. There is no nonzero-ring hypothesis: the prime argument is vacuous when there are no primes.

proof_origin.note: Direct compiled proof of the fibre argument of Stacks 07C0 using Mathlib tensor cancellation, localization equivalences and regular-ring local criterion. No new holes.

lean.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyRegular_fiber_of_localizations_maximal
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (h : ∀ (m : Ideal S) [m.IsMaximal],
      IsGeometricallyRegular p.ResidueField (p.Fiber (Localization.AtPrime m))) :
    IsGeometricallyRegular p.ResidueField (p.Fiber S)
